research_question: What published number describes dining activity at Worcester Commons, and does it establish average unique student attendance?

summary.recommended_metric_label: Reported daily meal volume during the academic year
summary.interpretation: Use the preferred record as a historical, approximate indicator of dining activity. It is not an audited attendance series or a count of distinct students.

reported_metrics.context: The article describes pandemic-era operations with traffic below the stated capacity.
reported_metrics.recommended_use: Historical service-capacity context only; do not substitute for measured demand.

reported_metrics.recommended_use: Historical service-capacity context only; do not substitute for measured demand.

metric_definitions.daily_meal_volume: Meals served over a day; the same diner can contribute multiple meals.
metric_definitions.daily_entry_count: Entries or transactions over a day; entry counts need not equal meals consumed.
metric_definitions.daily_unique_student_count: Distinct students who entered during a day, counted once per student across meal periods.
metric_definitions.simultaneous_occupancy: People physically present at one time; requires occupancy data or entries and exits.
metric_definitions.service_capacity: Stated ability to serve meals; does not establish actual demand.
metric_definitions.popularity_share: A defined share of comparable campus dining activity; requires matching counts for other locations.

data_quality.evidence_type: Published descriptive reports, not raw administrative data
data_quality.handling_of_discrepancy: Retain both source-specific claims. Do not average the figures or present either as measured attendance.
limitations: No sampling window or statistical averaging method is established for the preferred usage record.
A publication date does not identify the exact dates on which meals were counted.
Meals, entry transactions, distinct diners and simultaneous occupants are different metrics.
The student versus non-student breakdown is unavailable.
Service-outlet coverage within the building is not established.
No comparison dataset establishes a numeric popularity ranking among campus dining halls.
Historical descriptive values do not establish a current daily average.

appropriate_uses: Describe historical dining scale with source attribution and year.
Set a provisional simulation scenario, explicitly labeled as an assumption.
Motivate collection of real entry and meal-service records.
unsupported_uses: Treat meal volume as a distinct-student count.
Treat service capacity as observed daily attendance.
Assign invented breakfast, lunch, dinner or late-night shares.
Convert a daily total into peak occupancy without dwell-time and arrival data.
Present historical reports as measured attendance for November 13-20, 2026.

recommended_data_request.purpose: Establish average dining demand and student participation using observed records.
recommended_data_request.suggested_period: A complete recent teaching semester, with breaks, holidays and special events identified.

request_fields.description: Breakfast, lunch, dinner or late night, with period start and end times.
Aggregate entries or admissions, with the counting method documented.
Aggregate daily count of distinct students, deduplicated internally; no student identifiers requested.
Meals served if separately tracked, with the definition documented.
Separate main dining hall, Grab n Go, cafe and restaurant where applicable.
Optional 15- or 30-minute aggregate intervals for arrival patterns.
Weekday, weekend, holiday, break, special event or partial closure.

aggregation_rules: Average daily meals = sum of observed meals divided by included operating days.
Average unique students = sum of daily distinct student counts divided by included days.
Do not sum meal-period distinct student counts to obtain daily distinct students; the groups overlap.
Document whether closed days are included or excluded from each average.
Compare dining halls only over matching dates and outlet definitions.

null_value_policy: null means unavailable or not established by the reviewed sources, not zero.
provenance_note: Structured from public sources reviewed in this conversation. This file contains no newly measured attendance, invented meal-period allocation or raw swipe records.
